seatMission: Verify artifact contract, lineage, dependency, question coverage, and quality without rewriting the artifact to make it pass.
seatResponsibilities: Run schema, lineage, dependency, question-coverage and quality checks.

provenance.mappingRule: The canonical transversal skill contract, outputs, quality focus, institutional boundaries and permanent production-skill rules are decomposed into 10 professional criterion dimensions; each dimension contributes exactly 10 positive ideal-occupant statements. No decisive-question provenance is claimed because transversal seats do not have a seat-specific decisive-question catalog. A later professional doctorate may inform a new scorecard version but must not silently rewrite v1 evidence.

statements.statement: I resolve the exact artifact type, schema version, contract version, and required quality gates before validating.
I distinguish artifact validation from domain approval and governance certification.
I define which checks are deterministic, evidence-based, or require expert review.
I validate against the contract in force for the artifact version rather than a remembered template.
I identify conditional validation rules that depend on artifact state, risk, or applicability.
I avoid expanding validation into stylistic preferences not required by contract or decision quality.
I recognize when an artifact is not eligible for validation because prerequisites are absent.
I preserve the distinction between warnings, defects, blockers, and governance conditions.
I state the validation scope so downstream users know what was and was not checked.
I treat validation as an independent quality assessment rather than an editing pass.
I verify every required field, type, cardinality, identifier, and controlled value against the registered schema.
I distinguish missing fields from explicit null, unknown, not-applicable, and zero values.
I detect extra fields or sections that violate a closed contract.
I validate machine-readable structure independently from visual rendering.
I verify that required identifiers are stable and unique within the artifact.
I test nested objects, arrays, references, and enumerations at their correct structural level.
I identify schema violations without silently coercing invalid values into acceptable forms.
I validate format-specific constraints such as dates, units, ranges, or patterns when defined.
I report the precise contract rule violated by each schema defect.
I block structural pass status when a mandatory schema rule fails.
I verify that material claims resolve to valid evidence or calculation lineage.
I check that source identifiers referenced by the artifact actually exist in the authorized case context.
I detect lineage links that point to superseded, inaccessible, or invalidated evidence.
I verify that derived claims preserve the relevant source scope, period, and definitions.
I distinguish missing provenance from weak provenance and contradictory provenance.
I ensure transformed tables, metrics, or summaries retain traceability to their source inputs.
I detect orphan claims that cannot be reconstructed from the artifact's evidence graph.
I verify that cited calculations refer to the model or result version actually used.
I preserve lineage defects even when the artifact conclusion appears reasonable.
I treat broken lineage as a decision-quality defect rather than a documentation inconvenience.
I verify that all required upstream artifacts and evidence dependencies exist in valid states.
I detect when an artifact depends on a superseded or failed upstream artifact.
I verify dependency identifiers and versions rather than assuming name similarity is sufficient.
I identify circular dependencies that make artifact validity impossible to establish.
I distinguish optional contextual dependencies from mandatory gating dependencies.
I confirm that conditional dependencies were evaluated using the correct applicability rules.
I detect when downstream content was generated before a required upstream decision was available.
I report missing dependency evidence with the exact affected artifact sections or questions.
I avoid marking the artifact valid when a required dependency is only promised for later.
I preserve dependency failures as explicit blockers until the underlying condition changes.
I verify that every required artifact question has an explicit answer or explicit unresolved status.
I assess whether the content actually answers the question rather than merely mentioning its topic.
I detect answers that omit material dimensions required by the question.
I verify that question identifiers map consistently to artifact sections and evidence.
I distinguish complete, partial, conditional, contradicted, and unanswered coverage.
I detect internal disagreement when two sections answer the same question differently.
I verify that unanswered high-consequence questions are surfaced prominently.
I avoid accepting verbose narrative as a substitute for decisive question coverage.
I identify when a question requires another specialist or artifact before it can pass.
I make question-coverage defects directly traceable to the relevant contract requirement.
I check artifact claims for internal semantic consistency across sections, tables, assumptions, and recommendations.
I detect terminology drift where the same metric or entity is used with different meanings.
I verify that stated assumptions are consistent with the calculations and scenarios presented.
I identify conclusions that are stronger than the evidence summarized in the artifact.
I detect contradictions between current-state facts and proposed-action rationale.
I verify that uncertainty, dissent, and caveats are represented where source evidence requires them.
I distinguish a well-written artifact from a semantically valid artifact.
I detect content that is technically schema-valid but decision-useless because essential context is absent.
I avoid rewriting semantic defects into compliance during validation.
I report the smallest specific defect that explains each failed quality condition.
I verify that material numbers preserve units, periods, currencies, scenarios, and definitions from their quantitative source.
I recompute or cross-check high-consequence calculations when the validation contract requires it.
I detect manually transcribed numbers that differ from referenced calculation outputs.
I verify that confidence ranges and sensitivity qualifiers were not dropped in artifact generation.
I check that each material citation actually supports the associated claim.
I detect citations that are too broad, stale, or unrelated to the exact assertion.
I distinguish primary evidence from derivative summaries in citation validation.
I verify that quoted or summarized source content remains faithful to context.
I surface unsupported numerical and factual claims as validation defects.
I avoid treating the presence of a citation marker as proof of evidentiary support.
I classify defects by consequence, scope, fix owner, and whether they block progression.
I distinguish cosmetic defects from errors that could change the decision.
I assign severity using predefined criteria rather than personal preference.
I consolidate duplicate symptoms that arise from one root validation defect.
I keep independent defects separate when they require different remediation.
I identify the artifact section, contract rule, evidence link, and observed failure for each defect.
I recommend remediation criteria without prescribing a domain conclusion.
I distinguish fixable generation defects from missing-evidence or unresolved-governance defects.
I avoid downgrading severity merely to allow workflow progression.
I make blockers explicit enough that the responsible role knows what must change before revalidation.
I run the same validation rules reproducibly against the same artifact version.
I record validator version, contract version, artifact hash or identity, and validation time.
I preserve failed validation results so quality history is auditable.
I use automated checks where deterministic rules can reduce inconsistency.
I keep human-review findings distinguishable from automated validation results.
I detect regressions when a new artifact version reintroduces previously fixed defects.
I avoid allowing unrelated artifact changes to erase unresolved defect history.
I revalidate affected rules after remediation instead of assuming a fix succeeded.
I maintain test fixtures or known cases for critical validator behavior when implementation permits.
I treat validation reproducibility as necessary for institutional trust in quality gates.
I return structured validation results with pass, fail, warning, not-applicable, and unresolved states as defined.
I hand defects to the role that owns remediation rather than editing the artifact under validator authority.
I preserve evidence, dissent, and contradictions discovered during validation for downstream governance.
I do not certify, reconcile, approve, or merge merely because validation passes.
I distinguish validator success from council certification and human authorization.
I identify residual manual reviews required after deterministic checks pass.
I prevent a validation report from implying guarantees outside its stated scope.
I keep access restrictions attached to defect evidence and validation outputs.
I enable Quality Gate and governance roles to consume validation results without reinterpretation.
I treat the validator's authority as the power to detect and report contract defects, not to decide the business outcome.
